name: Tomato
notes: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; transplant out 1-2 weeks after last frost once soil has warmed.

name: Pepper
notes: Slow to germinate; start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Transplant only once nights stay above 55F, 1-3 weeks after last frost.

name: Eggplant
notes: Warm-season crop, similar timing to pepper; needs consistently warm soil (65F+) to transplant.

name: Cucumber
notes: Can be started indoors 3-4 weeks before transplanting, or direct-sown 1-2 weeks after last frost once soil is warm.

name: Zucchini
notes: Fast-growing squash; direct sow 1-3 weeks after last frost, or start indoors 2-3 weeks early for a head start.

name: Winter Squash
notes: Long season; direct sow after soil warms, or start indoors 3-4 weeks before last frost in short-season climates.

name: Pumpkin
notes: Direct sow 1-3 weeks after last frost; back-time from your first fall frost so the 90-120 day maturity window lands before it.

name: Watermelon
notes: Needs warm soil (65F+); start indoors 3-4 weeks before last frost, transplant 2-3 weeks after last frost.

name: Cantaloupe
notes: Same warm-soil requirements as watermelon; avoid disturbing roots when transplanting.

name: Corn
notes: Direct sow at last frost to 2 weeks after, once soil reaches 60F; does not transplant well. Succession sow every 2 weeks.

name: Green Bean
notes: Direct sow at last frost to 2 weeks after, once soil has warmed; frost-tender, do not rush.

name: Pea
notes: Cold-hardy; direct sow 4-6 weeks before last frost as soon as soil can be worked.

name: Lettuce

fallPlanting.notes: Second sowing for fall harvest 6-8 weeks before first fall frost; cold-tolerant, survives light frost.

notes: Cold-hardy; direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost. Also transplantable from indoor starts.

name: Spinach

fallPlanting.notes: Fall/overwintering sowing 6-8 weeks before first fall frost; very cold-hardy, tolerates hard frost.

notes: Very cold-hardy; direct sow 4-6 weeks before last frost as soon as soil can be worked.

name: Kale

fallPlanting.notes: Fall crop sown 8-10 weeks before first fall frost; flavor improves after light frost.

notes: Cold-hardy; direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost or start indoors for earlier transplants.

name: Arugula

fallPlanting.notes: Fast fall crop; sow 5-6 weeks before first fall frost.

notes: Fast-growing, cold-tolerant green; direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost, succession sow every 2-3 weeks.

name: Swiss Chard
notes: Fairly cold-hardy; direct sow 1-3 weeks before last frost. Tolerates light frost in fall too.

name: Broccoli

fallPlanting.notes: Fall crop: transplant 8-9 weeks before first fall frost (start seeds ~4 weeks before that).

notes: Start indoors 5-7 weeks before last frost; transplant out 2-3 weeks before last frost (hardens off to light frost).

name: Cauliflower

fallPlanting.notes: Fall crop is often more reliable than spring; transplant 9-10 weeks before first fall frost.

notes: Fussier than broccoli about temperature swings; start indoors 5-7 weeks before last frost, transplant 1-2 weeks before last frost.

name: Cabbage

fallPlanting.notes: Fall crop transplanted 8-10 weeks before first fall frost, matures in cool weather.

notes: Cold-hardy; start indoors 5-7 weeks before last frost, transplant 2-4 weeks before last frost.

name: Brussels Sprouts
notes: Long-season crop best timed to mature after a light fall frost for sweetest flavor; start indoors 5-7 weeks before last frost.

name: Carrot

fallPlanting.notes: Fall sowing 10-12 weeks before first fall frost; sweetens after light frost.

notes: Direct sow only (does not transplant); sow 2-4 weeks before last frost, as soon as soil can be worked.

name: Beet

fallPlanting.notes: Fall sowing 8-10 weeks before first fall frost.

notes: Direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost; tolerates light frost.

name: Radish

fallPlanting.notes: Fast fall crop; sow 4-6 weeks before first fall frost, can succession sow right up to first frost.

notes: Very fast and cold-hardy; direct sow 3-5 weeks before last frost, as soon as soil can be worked.

name: Turnip

fallPlanting.notes: Fall crop (often preferred) sown 8-10 weeks before first fall frost.

notes: Cold-hardy; direct sow 2-4 weeks before last frost.

name: Onion
notes: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost (or use sets/transplants); set out 2-4 weeks before last frost, very cold-tolerant as seedlings.

name: Garlic

fallPlanting.notes: Plant cloves 2-4 weeks before first fall frost so roots establish before ground freezes; harvest the following summer.

notes: Fall-planted crop only; not planted in spring in most climates.

name: Potato
notes: Plant seed potatoes 2-4 weeks before last frost, as soon as soil can be worked and is above 45F; light frost on emerging foliage is usually tolerated.

name: Sweet Potato
notes: Set out slips 2-4 weeks after last frost once soil is thoroughly warm (65F+); very frost/cold sensitive.

name: Asparagus
notes: Perennial; plant crowns 2-4 weeks before last frost as soon as soil can be worked. Takes 2-3 years to full production.

name: Basil
notes: Very frost/cold sensitive; start indoors 5-6 weeks before last frost, transplant only after all danger of frost (1-2 weeks after) and nights stay warm.

name: Cilantro

fallPlanting.notes: Cool-season herb; good fall sowing 6-8 weeks before first fall frost, bolts less in cool weather.

notes: Cool-season, bolts in heat; direct sow 1-3 weeks before last frost, succession sow through spring.

name: Parsley
notes: Slow to germinate; start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, transplant 1-2 weeks before last frost (biennial, cold-tolerant).

name: Dill
notes: Taprooted, does not transplant well; direct sow 1-3 weeks before last frost, succession sow through summer.

name: Oregano
notes: Perennial herb; start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, transplant around/just after last frost date.

name: Thyme
notes: Perennial herb, slow from seed; start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, transplant around/after last frost.

name: Sunflower
notes: Direct sow 1-3 weeks after last frost once soil has warmed; taprooted, resents transplanting.

name: Zinnia
notes: Frost-tender; direct sow 1-3 weeks after last frost, or start indoors 3-4 weeks early for earlier blooms.

name: Marigold
notes: Frost-tender; start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost, transplant after all frost danger has passed.

name: Cosmos
notes: Easy from direct seed 1-3 weeks after last frost; can also start indoors 3-4 weeks early.

name: Nasturtium
notes: Frost-tender, resents root disturbance; direct sow 1-3 weeks after last frost once soil has warmed.

name: Dahlia
notes: Plant tubers 1-3 weeks after last frost once soil is warm (60F+); very frost-sensitive.
